answers.value: I have been absent from the paddle for a few weeks due to other commitments.  I really enjoyed getting back on the CQQRS net this week.  Just the one QSO for me with Paul VK3KLE before I had to attend to other things.  A quick call sign, name, signal, QTH and rig exchange was just what I needed to open the door again.  Thanks Paul.  I plan to be back next week without (or perhaps just less) distractions.

The Ionosphere and my fellow operators certainly excelled themselves this week! Four Australians, one New Zealander, a Portuguese, and a German bounced their signal off the upper atmosphere and down onto a lonely figure sat in a damp English field. All excellent operators, especially considering some of them were struggling with poor conditions at their end. I salute you, gentlemen.
VK2IOW@20 VK2DBD@20 VK3DRQ@20 ZL3TK@20 VK3ACU@20 CT3BPF@20 DL3YZ@20
Nice to get a couple of quick contacts in after work tonight. I listened around while doing other things tonight. VK6 was prominent in stations heard here.
VK2TM, WA0VJD/VK5, VK7TO, VK7TA, VK6KHZ, VK2NNW, VK6GX, VK6AAV
Quite good conditions compared to previous weeks, as though the 40 m gods were welcoming the first night of spring,  despite it being only calendar-driven.

[20 m]
Strangeness continued to plague 20 m,  the first two EU stations were showing QRT on LSM and no sign of them on UK SDRs yet OM Manny was calling them, apparently he was able to hear things I could neither see nor hear.  Ross M0NNK was not detectable direct or on any UK SDR, then barely copyable on a German SDR,  yet he could hear me direct and I could hear myself in EU, however Ross rather quickly faded out from the Deutschland SDR so had to abandon the QSO without swapping reports.   Immediately following the aborted QSO with Ross,  heard Fabio IK0IXI calling CQ OC so answered on spec.  He reported my signal 579 near Roma, while his 1 kW into a four element beam was 421 here.  RX conditions seem consistently below par at this QTH, can't understand why but they always have been regardless of antenna type, either that or my expectations are simply too high.

[80 m]
Followed Lance VK7TO down to 80 m after 40 m became too noisy.   FB conditions, solid signals from all resulting in nice QSOs.   Finally made it on the FFA with a jolly persistent Stephen ZL3ABX, who was running only 2 watts;  it's called taking the 'low road'.  A satisfying night's work all told.
VK3DRQ@20   VK2IO  VK3AE VK6KD VK2KI VK1CT VK2IOW
160M was in great shape, Who is keen to have a go on 630m?
Tonight I was testing out a new Inverted Vee dipole. I was running 5W into it and the antenna worked great. The highlight of the night was working 2 VK6 stations.
Only two qsos, but a long session. Jim, wa0vjd/vk5, has just relocated to Adelaide so we may hear more from him, hopefully with a shorter callsign!
I only managed to have a brief time in the shack.  I was delighted when ZL3TK replied to my 2 Watt CQ QRS on 80 metres.   Didn't hear any other stations that were obviously part of the group.
Very low noise, very good conditions on 40m. Rig was vintage ft101e with vibroplex bug and additional weights added for qrs net.

From my portable location in Orange caravan park NSW I was blessed with S9 QRM so most of my recorded logs for Rx were through SDRs.  It was apparent the 40m was open right across  Oz from my location as I could hear my CQ echo coming back.  The band even got crowded as narrow band filtering would have been helpful to block out the stations on adjacent frequencies.  Still a great night on CW and good Rx practice.
Still experiencing S9 QRM at my portable location, I did achieve 1 QSO with Mark VK2KI.  QSB was also hampering my Rx signal but we struggled through with an exchange of RSN.
vk2ki vk3kle vk3wp vk5cw vk2tm wa0vjd vk2io/p vk5fd vk2nnw vk6gx vk2nnw vk3drq vk6aa vk3ech

[20m]
Hello everyone,
This is getting better every week!
Thanks M0NNK-Ross and VK6GX-Phil for the very nice QSO.

I'm always amazed at how my rig arrives in Australia!

Have a great week everyone.

73 Carlos - CT7BPF

[20m]  I was all set to listen for Willie DJ9FM, when he sent a message on Runner's Point, saying that the plumber had arrived early and he had to help fix the water supply.  Maybe next week.  I Had a nice QSO again with Ross M0NNK, though his signal was not as strong as that of last week.
[80m]  After dinner and after an interlude on 160m I had 2 QSOs, all good copy, VK1CT and VK2DLF.
[160m]  When I went back to the shack after dinner, Jordan VK3ACU sent a WhatsApp message saying there was DX on 160m.  I could hear AA1K, from Delaware, USA.  He must have a massive antenna; his signal varied in readabililty from 3 to 4.  I tried replying but my large horizontal loop and 100 watts was obviously not good enough.  After this I sent CQ and had a nice QSO with Jordan, both our signals were 599 plus 10 dB.  I guess the distance between us is about 650 km.
VK2KI, VK3DRQ, VK6KD/2, VK2IOW@160, VK3ACU@160, VK3NX@160

Great to have a go, nice to see it wasnt all about 5NN and on to the next one.  I did try calling CQ a few time but nothing back.  Maybe I should have posted in the WhatsApp group my freq when I was doing it.  Thanks to Paul and Gerarad for the QSO's

Nice to hear Paul VK3KLE's latest project on air;  the Yaesu FT-101E (which, like Holden cars, everyone had in the 70s) sounded great.  I then hooked up with Wal VK2WP at Bathurst who told me that he had been working on vintage radio restoration, like my neighbour SWL-Jack.  Wal was a solid S9 here.

A bit later listened in to Adam VK2NNW chatting to Phil VK6GX - hadn't heard Adam for yonks.  I then hooked up with Ron VK6KHZ South of Perth who reported my signal as RSN 522;  great to hear that Ron has got his noise problems sorted-out now.

[20m]
Well 20m conditions weren't great, but the turn-out from the CQQRS team certainly was!  I heard nine - and possibly 10 (I heard Ross M0NNK send the word "MANNY" at one stage - which I think meant he was talking to one VK3DRQ - who I couldn't quite hear - skip-zone and all that;  either that or Officer Ross was sending some sort of codeword.

Unfortunately Willie DJ9FM had plumbing troubles and couldn't join at the scheduled time - but did come up a bit later and was readable on Paul VK5PH's outstanding KiwiSDR at Ironstone Range;  I tried calling Willie, but signals were just too weak to make the connection.  Ross M0NNK portable somewhere was coming-in to Ironstone Range with a nice Q4 signal, but like Willie, wasn't making the grade on my Trio TS-120S crystal set.  Good to hear Jordan VK3ACU and Mike DL3YZ chatting to Ross, keeping him company in the lonely and probably cool moors.

When it was Carlos CT7BPF's turn, he also was very weak with me, but readable on the Ironstone Range KiwiSDR. 

[80m]
Down to 80m while everyone was having fun on 160m - my old Trio TS-120S doesn't go that low (it also doesn't go high either - it dies above 20m);  it's on the pile of work to be done!  Patrick VK2IOW had sent me a spare for parts - so really there's no excuse!

I was pleased as punch to be called by Peter VK5KDO at Encounter Bay.  It'd been over a year since we chatted last;  signals weren't great, but at least we got through again.  Next our travelling Sandgroper David VK6KD/2 called from the caravan park in Orange where the neighbouring grey nomads were generating an S9 noise level - so much for getting away from it all!  I was surprised that David's signal wasn't a bit stronger, considering the good band conditions - but it was good to catch up again.

After David, Georg VK2DLF up at St Marys really set my S-meter going;  it's been a long long time sine I saw an S9+30dB signal on the old girl.  Perhaps the temperature had something to do with it - Georg reported that it had been 28 degrees in Sydney;  pretty amazing for the first day of Spring.

I rounded out a nice evening's QRS with another S9 pair - Sava VK4PN up in Brisbane.  

Nice conditions - and lots of fun for me on Tuesday.

Condx seemed quite good, good signals from over east, Adam VK2NNW QRP > Dipole @ 25' 559.
Tried to persuade Rob, VK3ECH to sell me his TS-950SDX, but he wasn't having a bar of it.

CT7BPF@20
VU2USA@20
[20m]
Tried 20m for once, worked Carlos, CT7BPF, but too late for Willie and Ross, sorry guys! Had a nice QSO with Sam VU2USA immediately after Carlos.

[80] Late again, got on air at 11:50 UTC, bands deserted a single QSO in progress around 3535 KHz. Could recognize vk2ki keying not sure who was at the other end. Moved to 3530 and started calling CQ initially no luck but eventually Mark responded and we had a long Reg Chew. He mentioned he could see my signal at vk6bl SDR. I was monitoring my self at Ironstone, solid red so CONDX were excellent. Mark gave up after about half an our, his bed time he lamented , but  I continued calling until 13:00 HRS, no takers. At this stage I was monitoring myself at vk6bl and I was the only signal on air ( see SDR screen snippet ). Where were VK6 QRS netters, such a good opportunity to work across the continent. To make the missed opportunity even more painful after I moved to FT8 a number of vk6 stations were coming through quite strong. It was a great DX night as this late  east Asia, Siberia UA0 and UA9 and USA over the Pole were plentiful. For those who are into DX, 80m opens to EU and Africa  during the gray line around 19:00 UTC ( 5 am  QLD time ). Have a crack, even just hearing  such  DX on 80m is exciting.

I started calling CQ on 40 and was very excited to be answered by a new DXCC entity for me, Barry, YJ0BP, in Vanuatu.  We enjoyed a bit of a ragchew, with me telling him that if he was keen there was plenty of slow CW to be had down south, so am interested to see if anyone else worked him.  Next up was Ian, VK7TA.  We don't often get to work each other in the darker months being at opposite ends of the state, yet still rather close, so it was nice to catch up and work a station sharing similar WX.  Paul, VK3KLE and I had our second QSO in as many weeks with a brief hello.  My final contact on 40 was with Stan, ZL3TK.  Unfortunately after starting well my noise floor started increasing to the point where after several overs it was getting hard to hear.  My neighbours have just returned home after several months away, and brought evening QRM with them.  Fortunately we get on well so don't expect it will be too hard to resolve.  None the less, I left 40 and went searching for quieter spectrum.

After calling for several minutes on 80, who should answer my call, but a much more easily copyable Stan again.  We managed to conclude our QSO in far more ear pleasing fashion.  

As I write this and gaze across at my radio on 40, I see my noise floor is once again sitting at around S2, that's more like it.
I had to work this morning, but hat some time to send some beeps during a short break. Thanks for the beeps :-) 73 Mike

Manny, VK6DRQ, always comes in as a strong signal here at Esperance. My signal is obviously weak at his end as I do not get a reply when I answer his CQ's. This week however he heard my signal and we had a QSO on 80 metres. Mind you I had to send each word 3 times as his report of my signal was RSN 332. I found getting that RSN made it clear I was just making above the noise into Blackburn Victoria.

He had not heard me on 40 metres. I then moved to 80 metres after finding 40 completely chockers with signals, many just a few hundred Hz apart, and there was Manny again calling CQ.
VK6HRC  VK6BEK  VK6AA  VK6IS  VK6NC  VK6JDM  VK2KI

Conditions on 20m were quite alright. All the stations I did call, I had an answer except OM Carlos. I did heard him only on the South Australia SDR, nil on the RX and after calling him several times he said he could not copy me.
CT7BPF@20, IO0UXQ@20, VK2GR@20, VK2IOW@20, VK2KI@20, VK3ACU@20, VK3ADT@20, VK3DBD@20, VK6GX@20, VK7TA@20.
VK5KFG, VK6JDM, VK6NQL DL3YZ@20, EA2AJB@20, M0NNK@20.
Beautiful South Bowning NSW, but listening via the VK6BL KiwiSDR at Mount Barker
This week I listened in to the KiwiSDR belonging to Bevan VK6BL at Mount Barker.  Interesting that David VK6KD/2 was only S-5 to me direct, but was coming through ok to Mount Barker.

I came in a bit late to the night and started tuning around 40m but there was little there but noise.  So I followed the whatsapp messages to 80m where I was lucky to hear a couple of QSOs between VK2KI with VK6KD/2 and VK2DLF.  I also heard a partial QSO with a VK5 which I noted as VK5KDO but I have little confidence in that.
It was good to hear the activity on the bands and have the opportunity to try to copy the CW being sent, it even felt like I was copying more than previous weeks so maybe I am improving... 
I then went up to 160m, an area of the bands I have very rarely ventured, mostly because I only have a 40m long antenna.  But I could hear a one sided QSO and even tried to put out a short CQ.  In trying to tune my antenna, it was a solid 1:1 without any tuner which while initially sounding good, may also mean it is an effective dummy load on 160m.  So I was back to listening on the bands.
Thank you all again for such an active morse group.
